does: Cuts the backbone out of a whole bird and presses it flat, so that it cooks quickly and evenly and all of its skin faces the heat.

intro.what: Spatchcocking takes out the backbone of a whole bird and flattens it.
intro.why: A flat bird cooks in about half the time, the legs and breast finish together, and every part of the skin can crisp.

how: Set the bird breast side down on a board, with the tail towards you.
Cut along both sides of the backbone with strong kitchen scissors and lift it out. Keep it for stock.
Turn the bird over, open it out like a book and press hard on the breastbone with the heel of your hand until it cracks and the bird lies flat.
Tuck the wing tips behind the breast so that they do not burn.

cues.text: The breastbone gives with a dull crack when you press on it.
The bird lies flat, legs splayed out, with the thighs and breast at an even height.

mistakes.mistake: Cutting with a knife and slipping on the bones.
mistakes.fix: Use strong kitchen scissors and cut close to the backbone.

mistakes.mistake: Leaving the bird arched, so the breast cooks faster than the legs.
mistakes.fix: Press on the breastbone until it lies truly flat.

quiz.question: Why is a bird spatchcocked before it is grilled or roasted?
choices: So that it cooks faster and more evenly, with all the skin facing the heat.
So that it holds a stuffing.
So that it can be cooked from frozen.
quiz.because: Flat, the bird is an even thickness and its whole skin side meets the heat.

quiz.question: Which side of the backbone do you cut?
choices: Both sides, so that the backbone comes out.
Neither: you cut through the breast.
quiz.because: The backbone is cut out along both sides; the breastbone stays and is pressed flat.

quiz.question: What tells you the bird has been pressed flat enough?
choices: It still rocks on the board.
The breastbone cracks and the bird lies flat.
quiz.because: A dull crack and a level bird show the breastbone has given way.

quiz.question: Your bird browned well at the breast but the thighs lagged behind. What would you change?
choices: Press it flatter before cooking so the legs and breast sit level.
Cook it breast side down only.
quiz.because: A bird left arched cooks unevenly; pressing it flat evens the thickness.

variant_of.differs: It opens a whole bird, cut along the back with scissors and pressed flat on the breastbone, where butterflying opens a small fish along the belly with a knife.
